answer: Each grading pool carries five honeypot answers, tagged with a seed-derived pigment the jury can read but submitters cannot, and they sit at random among the honest entries. A farm that attests in bulk has to score those plants as well: pass one and its bond is slashed 25 POA on the spot. With five plants in a hundred answers, blind attestation collides roughly once in twenty, an expected loss of 1.25 POA against a 0.4 POA reward, so only an agent that actually reads every entry survives. In an oasis of prose the sparrow pecks each seed and leaves the painted gravel alone.
